14. The Domestic Violence Act emphasizes the need for a fair hearing.
Ex-parte relief may be granted in urgent situations, but the principle of natural justice requires that all parties have an opportunity to present their case.
The Act does not support granting relief without hearing the respondent unless there is a compelling reason to do so.

Thus, the issuance of an ex-parte order directing him to remove his belongings from 2 nd floor of the property without hearing him violates the principles of natural justice.
Further, at the time of granting ex-parte relief, the court is required to assess whether the respondent/complainant demonstrated a genuine sense of urgency warranting ex-parte relief.
The absence of imminent danger or a credible threat to the respondent's safety raises concerns about the necessity of immediate judicial intervention.
The order passed by learned MM appears to reflect a mechanical manner rather than a reasoned approach.
